prompt.context: Your client is AlphaKeni, a BPO enterprise that helps various businesses outsource their customer service operations. The business has been experiencing a declining customer satisfaction rating, owing to which it has been losing business to competition. The CEO has engaged you to understand what is driving this trend and how it can be remedied.
prompt.question: What is driving the decline in customer satisfaction at AlphaKeni, and how can it be remedied?

clarifying_info.a: AlphaKeni has operations only in South Asia — India, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka.

clarifying_info.q: What types of calls does AlphaKeni handle?
clarifying_info.a: The scope of operations is only to service inbound calls regarding reservations, tech support, loyalty programs, and baggage assistance.

clarifying_info.q: What industries or clients does AlphaKeni serve?
clarifying_info.a: The business specializes in serving clients in the commercial aviation space, such as British Airways, Etihad, Emirates, Air France, etc.

clarifying_info.q: How much have satisfaction scores dropped?
clarifying_info.a: Customer satisfaction scores have progressively dropped from a high of 82 in 2015 to 68 in 2017. AlphaKeni is seeking to raise its satisfaction scores back to 2015 levels.

exhibits.title: Average Customer Wait Time by Company
exhibits.shows: A bar chart comparing average customer wait time (in minutes) across Competitor 1, Competitor 2, Competitor 3, and AlphaKeni. Wait time is defined as the time it takes for a customer to connect with an agent who can address their needs.

exhibits.title: Ratio of Hourly Calls to Call Center Associates
exhibits.shows: A bar chart comparing the ratio of number of hourly calls to call center associates across Competitor 1, Competitor 2, Competitor 3, and AlphaKeni.

exhibits.title: Illustration of Application Funnel
exhibits.shows: A funnel diagram showing the number of applicants at each stage of AlphaKeni's hiring process. Note: this exhibit is for illustrative purposes only to help understand how the application funnel works.

exhibits.title: Benchmarking Data: Hiring Funnel and Attrition vs. Competitors
exhibits.shows: A table benchmarking AlphaKeni against three competitors (A, B, C) across hiring funnel conversion rates, quarterly attrition rate, and average annual pay per associate.

framework: Understand the root cause of declining customer satisfaction — start with what customers experience (wait time, resolution quality) and work backward
Benchmark AlphaKeni's operational metrics against competitors to identify gaps
Investigate operational drivers: technology, staffing levels, demand forecasting, and agent quality/training
Investigate people/talent drivers: hiring funnel efficiency, compensation, attrition, and workforce planning
Synthesize findings and prioritize the highest-impact lever
Develop recommendations with near-term and longer-term actions

questions.prompt: After reviewing Exhibit 1, what does the data tell you, and what hypotheses do you form about the root cause?
questions.guidance: A strong candidate will immediately observe that AlphaKeni's average wait time (~4.5 min) is dramatically higher than all three competitors (1–2 min). They should generate multiple hypotheses: (1) Outdated/slow technology reducing throughput; (2) Poor agent training leading to longer handle times; (3) Poor demand forecasting causing understaffing during peak periods; (4) Understaffed call centers — either insufficient hiring or high turnover. The candidate should propose to prioritize these and identify what data would prove or disprove each.

questions.prompt: After reviewing Exhibit 2 (calls-to-associates ratio), what does this tell you about the staffing situation?
questions.guidance: AlphaKeni's calls-to-associate ratio (~38) is roughly 2–3x its competitors (~12–20), confirming severe understaffing relative to call volume. The candidate should connect this to the high wait times observed in Exhibit 1 and focus the analysis on why AlphaKeni is understaffed — is it a supply problem (not enough hires) or a retention problem (people leaving too fast)?

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2 (Application Funnel) and Exhibit 3 (Benchmarking), diagnose why AlphaKeni's call centers are understaffed.
questions.guidance: Key insight: AlphaKeni actually outperforms or matches competitors on every funnel conversion rate (language test 65% vs 60-64%; computer test 57% vs 50-54%; background check 89% comparable to 90-93%; acceptance rate 86% vs 74-84%). This rules out the hiring funnel as the problem. However, AlphaKeni's quarterly attrition rate (92%) is dramatically higher than competitors (73-86%) despite paying the highest average salary ($6,800 vs $5,000-$6,500). Since salary is the most important factor for applicants (per industry survey) and AlphaKeni leads on pay, the high attrition is not driven by compensation. The candidate should infer that the root cause is either: (a) poor job-fit sourcing — employees self-selecting out because the role does not match expectations; or (b) incorrect applicant assessment — employees being dismissed for performance reasons. Either way, the hiring/assessment process is sending the wrong people into roles they cannot or will not retain.

math.setup: Illustrative only — to understand funnel output vs. attrition. Starting from 30,000 applications, track offers accepted and compare to attrition impact.
steps: × 75% offer acceptance = 6,800 new hires per cohort
With 92% quarterly attrition, roughly 92% of the existing workforce leaves each quarter, meaning almost all net new hires are offset by departures — the workforce never grows meaningfully
math.answer: High attrition (92% quarterly) wipes out hiring gains and keeps the associate base chronically below what is needed to handle call volume, driving up calls-per-associate and wait times.

questions.prompt: Brainstorm: What could be causing AlphaKeni's abnormally high attrition rate despite the highest pay in the market?

brainstorming.prompt: Given that AlphaKeni pays the highest salary yet has the highest attrition, what are possible root causes of the high attrition, and what solutions could address them?

categories.name: Sourcing / Job-Fit Issues
ideas: Recruiting from candidate pools that are not well-suited for call center work (e.g., over-qualified candidates who leave quickly)
Job descriptions that misrepresent the nature of the work, creating expectation mismatch
Geographic sourcing limited to areas with higher-opportunity alternatives, so employees leave for better roles

categories.name: Assessment / Selection Process Issues
ideas: Current tests (language + computer skills) do not assess soft skills critical for call center roles (e.g., patience, empathy, stress tolerance)
No simulation or role-play in the interview process to screen for real job performance
Employees being asked to leave due to poor performance that could have been screened out upfront

categories.name: Onboarding and Training Issues
ideas: Inadequate onboarding leaving new associates ill-equipped to handle calls, leading to early exits
Insufficient ramp support causing high early-tenure attrition within first 90 days

categories.name: Work Environment / Culture Issues
ideas: High call-to-associate ratio creates excessive workload pressure, burning out agents
Lack of career development pathways or promotion opportunities
Poor supervisory quality or management practices

categories.name: Solutions
ideas: Redesign sourcing channels to target candidates with demonstrated stability and aptitude for repetitive customer service roles
Introduce behavioral/soft-skills assessments and realistic job previews in hiring funnel
Add structured 90-day onboarding and performance coaching programs
Reduce workload per agent by expanding headcount (virtuous cycle once attrition is reduced)
Conduct stay interviews and exit interviews to pinpoint specific attrition drivers

recommendation: AlphaKeni's declining customer satisfaction is driven by abnormally long wait times (~4.5 min vs. competitor range of 1–2 min), which stem from a calls-to-associate ratio approximately 2–3x higher than peers

The root cause is chronic understaffing caused by a quarterly attrition rate of 92% — the highest in the industry — despite AlphaKeni paying the highest average salary ($6,800 vs. $5,000–$6,500 for competitors)

Since funnel conversion rates are comparable to or better than peers, the problem is not attracting or screening applicants: the problem is that the wrong candidates are being hired or assessed, leading to rapid departure

We recommend AlphaKeni focus immediately on (1) diagnosing attrition root cause through exit interviews and stay surveys, and (2) redesigning the assessment process to screen for soft skills and job-fit, not just language and computer skills
risks: Attrition may have multiple simultaneous causes (sourcing, assessment, work environment) that require a bundled intervention rather than a single fix
Reducing the calls-to-associate ratio requires increasing headcount, which takes time — customer satisfaction improvement will lag behind any hiring/assessment fix
Competitors may also be improving their operations, raising the bar AlphaKeni must meet to recapture satisfaction scores
next_steps: Conduct exit interviews and stay interviews to empirically identify the primary attrition driver(s)
Audit the current language and computer skills tests; add structured behavioral assessments and realistic job previews
Pilot a revised hiring process in one geography and measure 90-day retention vs. current baseline
Set headcount targets based on required calls-to-associate ratio to reach competitor-level wait times
Track customer satisfaction scores monthly as a lagging indicator of operational improvement
